notes.W4400490766: Serial blood samples taken yearly for up to 15 years before diagnosis let them time when each driver mutation arrived and measure its fitness. The first drivers appear decades early and grow slowly. Later drivers carry up to 100-fold larger advantages and can take over the whole blood years before leukaemia shows. Pre-cancer turns out to follow simple, quantifiable evolutionary rules.
notes.W2805780137: A formal model of why smart people keep a wrong model despite plenty of data: if you only attend to the variables your model says matter, the evidence that would refute it never registers. It explains stable errors without assuming irrationality. It applies directly to scientific blind spots, clinical habits and markets.
notes.W4400480772: Electron flow in graphene can behave like a viscous fluid, but viscosity had never been measured cleanly. A Corbino-geometry device separates the ohmic and viscous parts of transport. Scattering scales linearly with temperature, not quadratically as standard Fermi-liquid theory predicts. That supports a newly predicted 'tomographic' fluid regime.
notes.W7225127387: A randomised trial in moderate aortic stenosis, a group normally just monitored. TAVR cut death or heart-failure events at two years from 23.9% to 16.7%. Caveat: open-label, all-cause death was not lower, and the composite outcome includes softer heart-failure events.
notes.W4286895426: This settles a decades-old Almgren conjecture: area-minimising surfaces can have fractal singular sets, and you can choose the structure of those singularities. It's a sharp answer to how badly 'optimal' geometric objects can behave, a basic question behind soap films and minimal surfaces.
notes.W7125966085: Type Ia supernovae, the standard candles behind dark energy, seem to come in two populations with different colours and light-curve standardisation, not one. Modelling them separately tightens the cosmological constraints and removes a long-standing host-galaxy-mass correction for unreddened supernovae. This bears directly on the current debate over evolving dark energy.
notes.W4399758823: A field-defining review of computing gradients through differential-equation models: adjoint methods, automatic differentiation and hybrid physics-ML models. It's the mathematical machinery behind fitting simulations to data. Read it as the map for the inverse-problem side of simulation-based work.
notes.W7161720390: An analytic explanation of where a black hole's ringdown series (its quasinormal modes) stops converging. The cause is a singularity in complex time, created by a light ray that bounces off the black-hole singularity. It's a rare case of the interior geometry setting a limit on what outside observers can expand.
notes.W4390843425: Natural experiments in Florida show climate risk is mispriced through a weak link: under-capitalised home insurers that the mortgage agencies accept without pricing their risk. Insurer collapses causally increase mortgage defaults after disasters. Lenders lend more freely when they can pass the risk on to taxpayers. It shows how hidden risk concentrates in practice.
notes.W4417398541: A consensus atlas of 1.8 million nuclei across human, macaque and marmoset basal ganglia. It identifies 61 cell types conserved over 76 million years and pins psychiatric and neurodegenerative risk genes to specific cell populations. Spatial identity turns out to be more conserved than the classic D1/D2 split.

thread: Two of today's picks are about systems that hide their own failure modes. In the leukaemia paper, blood looks normal while a slow evolutionary takeover runs for decades. In the insurance paper, markets look stable while risk quietly pools in fragile insurers. The attention paper supplies the reason both go unseen: the signal never registers if you aren't tracking the variable that carries it.

notes.W4416048293: Shifts: Huang and Yang's 1957 formula for a dilute Fermi gas was a physicist's prediction → now a theorem, valid for a broad class of interactions through the scattering length alone. A 68-year-old universality claim now has a proof.
notes.W4417295272: Shifts: how many uses it takes to learn an unknown quantum process to a given precision (in the standard diamond-distance metric) was a long-standing open question → now answered optimally. This is a basic limit on what we can know about a quantum device.
notes.W7225771350: Shifts: ecosystem tipping points described phenomenologically → derived from local trade-offs between individual plants using phase-transition theory. Macroscopic collapse becomes a consequence of microscopic rules, the same move statistical physics made for matter.
notes.W4411476832: Shifts: microbial community dynamics assumed irreducibly complex, driven by myriad interactions → observable dynamics turn out to be low-dimensional, with linear scaling. That would explain why control from a handful of measurements works at all.
notes.W7154510137: Shifts: the universal anomalous scaling seen in QCD power corrections was an empirical regularity → traced to its operator origin in quantum field theory via light-ray operators. A pattern gets a mechanism, which is what turns a fit into physics.

foundation.title: Microscopic detail washes out into few variables
foundation.principle: Several of today's papers turn out to be the same claim: complex systems are governed by far fewer effective variables than their parts suggest. A dilute Fermi gas's energy depends on the interaction only through one number, the scattering length. A decade of blood evolution before leukaemia follows a few simple rules of mutation timing and fitness. Microbial communities with countless interactions trace low-dimensional paths. A dryland ecosystem's collapse is a phase transition set by local trade-offs. This compression is why science works at all, why a few observables can predict and control a system. The live question is where it fails.
rests_on: P. W. Anderson (1972). More Is Different
K. G. Wilson (1971). Renormalization Group and Critical Phenomena
Machta, Chachra, Transtrum, Sethna (2013). Parameter Space Compression Underlies Emergent Theories and Predictive Models
foundation.question: Can we tell in advance whether a system will compress to a few variables or stay irreducibly high-dimensional? A rare leukaemia driver or a single tipping event may be exactly where the compression breaks.

W4400490766.question: What evolutionary rules govern the years of pre-cancerous change before acute myeloid leukaemia?
W4400490766.approach: Deep duplex sequencing of annual blood samples taken up to 15 years before diagnosis, interpreted with evolutionary theory.
W4400490766.finding: First drivers arise decades early and grow slowly. Later drivers give up to 100-fold larger advantages and can sweep the blood.
W4400490766.implication: Pre-leukaemic evolution is quantifiable, follows simple rules, and leaves signals years before diagnosis.

W2805780137.question: Why do people keep mistaken beliefs despite high stakes, abundant data and repeated chances to learn?
W2805780137.approach: A formal model where attention is channelled through a person's possibly misspecified model of the world.
W2805780137.finding: Some wrong models are 'attentionally stable': the data a person attends to never reveals the error.
W2805780137.implication: Persistent error can come from what we notice, not irrational reasoning. This reframes learning failures in people and institutions.

W4400480772.question: Can the viscosity of electron fluids in 2D materials be measured quantitatively?
W4400480772.approach: Magnetoresistance in Corbino-shaped graphene devices, used as a combined ohmmeter and viscometer.
W4400480772.finding: In monolayer and bilayer graphene, electron scattering scales linearly with temperature, not the T² Fermi-liquid theory predicts.
W4400480772.implication: Supports a predicted 'tomographic' fluid regime that may be generic to two-dimensional electron systems.

W7225127387.question: Does early TAVR beat surveillance in moderate aortic stenosis with at-risk features?
W7225127387.approach: International open-label randomised trial: transfemoral TAVR vs clinical surveillance, 1:1, death or heart-failure event at 2 years.
W7225127387.finding: Primary endpoint 16.7% vs 23.9% (difference −7.2 points, 95% CI −13.1 to −1.3). All-cause death 8.4% vs 7.3%.
W7225127387.implication: May move intervention earlier in aortic stenosis, though mortality was not reduced.

W4286895426.question: How irregular can the singular set of an area-minimising submanifold be?
W4286895426.approach: Explicit construction of area-minimising submanifolds on compact Riemannian manifolds.
W4286895426.finding: Singular sets can be fractal, with any prescribed Almgren stratification. The result is sharp in dimension.
W4286895426.implication: Settles Almgren's conjecture and marks the limits of regularity theory for minimal surfaces.

W7125966085.question: Do Type Ia supernovae form one standardisable population, or several?
W7125966085.approach: The updated UNITY1.8 Bayesian model applied to the Union3.1 compilation, allowing two populations.
W7125966085.finding: The two populations differ in light-curve shape, colour and standardisation. The host-mass step vanishes for unreddened supernovae, and uncertainties shrink.
W7125966085.implication: Supernova cosmology, central to the dark-energy debate, needs standardisation that accounts for both populations.

W4399758823.question: How should gradients be computed through models built on differential equations?
W4399758823.approach: A review of differentiable programming for differential equations, spanning inverse methods and machine learning.
W4399758823.finding: Sets out the methods and trade-offs for sensitivity analysis, parameter inversion and hybrid physics–ML models.
W4399758823.implication: Gives simulation, inverse problems and machine learning one shared mathematical toolkit.

W7161720390.question: What sets where a Schwarzschild black hole's quasinormal-mode expansion converges?
W7161720390.approach: Analytic study of the singularities of the retarded Green's function in complex time.
W7161720390.finding: Convergence is bounded by a 'bouncing singularity' from a light ray reflecting off the black-hole singularity.
W7161720390.implication: The black hole's interior geometry limits what ringdown expansions seen from outside can describe.

W4390843425.question: How is climate risk mispriced through property insurance and mortgages?
W4390843425.approach: Natural experiments on a new Florida dataset linking mortgages and insurers, 2009–2018.
W4390843425.finding: Fragile insurers' insolvency causally raises post-disaster defaults. Mortgage-agency practices put ~25% of their expected Florida losses on insurer fragility.
W4390843425.implication: Hidden insurer weakness passes climate risk to taxpayers. Screening insurance quality would change who gets credit.

W4417398541.question: What is a unified cross-species taxonomy of basal ganglia cell types?
W4417398541.approach: Multiomic consensus atlas of 1.8 million nuclei from humans, macaques and marmosets across eight structures.
W4417398541.finding: 61 homologous cell types conserved over 76 million years. Dorsal-ventral identity is more conserved than the D1/D2 split.
W4417398541.implication: A reference map for basal ganglia evolution and disease, pinning psychiatric risk to specific cell types.

figure_notes.W4286895426: One step of the construction: a flat piece spanned by the y₁, y₂ and x₃ directions is pushed out along y₃, controlled by a function f. Deformations like this are the authors' tool for dictating where, and how intricately, the surface fails to be smooth.
figure_notes.W7125966085: Rows are redshift bins. Columns are corrected brightness, light-curve shape (x₁) and colour (c). Thin blue lines are the older single-population model, thick black the new two-population model, and points are the data coloured by misfit. Where black tracks the points better, such as the faster cut-off at high x₁, the second population is real structure.
figure_notes.W4399758823: A two-axis map of every way to get gradients through a differential-equation solver. Left–right: differentiate the solver's discrete steps (automatic differentiation) or solve a new continuous equation (adjoints). Up–down: push sensitivities forward from inputs or backward from outputs. Use it as a decision chart.
figure_notes.W7161720390: A spacetime picture of the black-hole response to a point source (black dot). The response is built differently in different regions, and the boundary sits at the radius where the light cone scatters off the black hole's potential. The paper's job is to explain why that boundary sits exactly there: the bouncing singularity.
figure_notes.W4417295272: The learning pipeline, left to right: feed one half of entangled pairs through the unknown channel, purify the resulting Choi-state copies, learn them with optimal pure-state tomography, then project the estimate onto valid quantum channels. The output is within ε of the truth in diamond distance, with optimal channel uses.
